subject: Post-call recap + request: Avery Health bakeoff & next-step ops
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Peter Liu <peter.liu@averyhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + request: Avery Health bakeoff & next-step ops

Hi Peter — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the asks we discussed so we can keep momentum.

Key pain points you called out:
- High inference cost with current provider at scale (spikes when batch jobs run).
- Latency variability on 2–4 second 95th percentile for conversational workloads.
- Inconsistent embeddings between model variants (impacts reranking / semantic search).
- Need for predictable isolation and audit logs for PHI-adjacent workloads.

Top goals you want to achieve in the next 3 months:
1) Proof-of-concept that demonstrates 30–40% cost reduction per 1M tokens while keeping 95p latency under 800ms for single-turn queries.
2) Embedding parity (<=3% delta on similarity scoring) vs your current baseline for the 50k query set.
3) A short security checklist and architecture diagram that satisfies your InfoSec for an initial trial.

Immediate asks / next steps we agreed:
- Redwood to run a head-to-head bakeoff vs their incumbent (NimbusAI) on a representative subset of queries and provide numeric comparatives (latency distribution, cost/unit, embedding drift).
- Provide an initial test plan and runbook for your infra/security review.
- Coordinate a short POC (2 weeks) with Avery's security and SRE teams; tentative start the week of Apr 4.

Attachments / links: attached the meeting recording and the requirements matrix you filled out in the call (avery_requirements_matrix.xlsx). I also added the Drive folder link for shared artifacts.

Open questions I flagged on the call (so we don't forget):
- Which specific API keys / data redaction controls will your SRE want for the POC?
- Do you want us to include a quantized LLM variant in the bakeoff for cost comparison?
- Any hard SLA/uptime limits required for the evaluation environment?

I'll follow up internally and loop in engineering to scope the comparison and the test harness. Proposed owner for the run: Jonas.

Thanks — Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference
From: Peter Liu <peter.liu@averyhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@averyhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + request: Avery Health bakeoff & next-step ops

Camila — thanks for the tidy recap. Confirming the priorities below and a couple clarifications:

1) Cost is top priority but cannot come at >10% degradation in ranking quality for our top 500 queries.
2) Latency target is 95p < 800ms for single-turn, but for multi-turn sessions we'd accept up to 1.2s while we investigate KV caching.
3) Security: Alex (cc'd) will own the checklist and will want an architecture diagram and SOC-2 evidence before signing off.

We're happy to run the POC window Apr 4–16; Alex and I will reserve SRE time for April 4–5 to help onboard.

Two asks from our side: can you include the incumbent NimbusAI in the bakeoff and a third open-source quantized variant so we can see cost curves? Also please call out tokenization differences (they matter for our billing model).

I'll loop Alex into the drive link. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

–Peter

--
Peter Liu
Director, Data & AI Platforms
Avery Health
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap + request: Avery Health bakeoff & next-step ops

Team — forwarding the prospect confirmation. TL;DR: Avery wants a 2-week POC Apr 4–16, includes incumbent (NimbusAI) + an open-source quantized baseline in the comparison. They care about cost delta, 95p latency, and embedding parity.

Action items for engineering/run team (Jonas, can you lead):
- Produce a short bakeoff plan with exact input sets: use their 50k query subset + the top 500 ranking sample (we have the matrix in the Drive).
- Run head-to-head: Redwood (prod config we usually use for trials) vs NimbusAI (their baseline) vs an open-source quantized model (recommend llama-quant-8bit or similar).
- Metrics: median/95/99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), cost estimate per 1M tokens (include VM/GPU amortized), embedding cosine drift against their baseline, and failure/error modes.
- Include KV/prefix cache test: cold vs warm runs to capture caching benefit.
- Deliverable: spreadsheet with numeric results + short README with test harness and exact command lines.

Constraints/notes:
- They asked for tokenization normalization reporting — call this out in the README so we show how we computed per-token cost.
- Security: we need to prepare a SOC-2 evidence packet and a minimal architecture diagram for Alex; Marissa can you coordinate with Security for the checklist items?

Attachments: I attached our bakeoff runbook draft (redwood-bakeoff-runbook.md) and the meeting recording for context.

Can you respond with a one-page run plan and an estimated timeline today? If we can commit by EOD we can hit the Apr 4 start date.

Thanks,
Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap + request: Avery Health bakeoff & next-step ops

Got it — I'll own the test harness. Quick acknowledgement and plan:

Plan (summary):
- Day 0 (Mar 29): finalize dataset slices (50k + top500) and confirm tokenization baseline.
- Day 1–3 (Apr 4–6): run baseline (NimbusAI) and Redwood standard config; capture latency and throughput under identical load patterns.
- Day 4–6 (Apr 7–9): run quantized model comparison + cold/warm cache experiments.
- Day 7–9 (Apr 10–12): embedding parity tests + similarity scoring; produce numbers and plots.
- Day 10 (Apr 13): compile spreadsheet + README + short slide with decision bullets.

Deliverables: run results spreadsheet (CSV), runbook (redwood-bakeoff-runbook.md), and a 1-page summary slide. I'll also include tokenization normalization logs and the exact CLI commands we ran.

I'll need a small Dedicated test slot (2 GPUs for burst workload) and permission to spin up the NimbusAI baseline in their sandbox (we have an account they shared previously). Estimated engineering effort: 2.5 engineer-days.

I'll drop the one-page run plan into the Drive folder and ping when ready.

–Jonas
